value:
wf_word_diff.py MEASURES THE RAW PRE-POSTPROCESS BODY - it says so in its own output line, `(raw postprocess body)` - WHILE fndiff, fnasm --ours, probe.py and defake_gate all read the POSTPROCESSED object. On a webfrank-pinned function the two therefore disagree by construction and in a specific, misleading direction: the word count reports the residual the pin ALREADY CLOSES, so a queue ranked by differing words puts FINISHED functions at the top.

This is the INVERSE of the hazard AGENTS.md discipline 10 already warns about. That warning is 'pinned functions read real 0 by construction, so screen the pins before ranking by real'. The word count fails the opposite way: pinned functions read a LARGE residual by construction. A lane that switched from `real` to the word count on the strength of claim.law.identical-multiset-is-blind-to-displacements.20260831.v1 - which is the right move for the metric - lands straight in the mirror-image trap, and the pin screen it was told to run for `real` is exactly as mandatory here.

MEASURED THIS RUN, and it is not a marginal effect. Of the 8 functions the run-39 census classified into the recolor class by raw word count, HALF - 4 of 8, carrying 209 of the class's 355 differing words - were already webfrank-pinned and closed. Ranked by word count they occupied first, third, fifth and eighth place, including the top row. The tell that saves the lane is free and unambiguous: build the target-to-ours callee-saved correspondence from `fnasm --ours`; a pinned-and-closed function yields the IDENTITY map with zero unexplained operand pairs while its word count is large. Identity map + large word count = you are reading a shipped rule's input, not an open residual.

THE SCREEN, in order, before ranking anything by differing words: (1) parse `config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json` - note the rules live under the top-level `units` key, not at the root, and a parser that iterates the root finds 2 keys and 0 pins rather than 50 keys and 142 pins, which reads exactly like 'no pins exist'; (2) drop every function that appears as a rule `function` there; (3) only then rank. The same screen also fixes the reverse question - the correct customer census for a postprocessor capability must be taken over the SURVIVING set, because a pinned function is not a customer for the capability that already serves it.
